```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)
```

```{r}
nyc_airbnb = 
  nyc_airbnb |>
  mutate(
    stars = review_scores_location / 2
  ) |>
  rename(
    borough = neighbourhood_group
  ) |>
  filter(
    borough != "Staten Island"
  ) |>
  select(price, stars, borough, neighbourhood, room_type) 

nyc_airbnb
```
```{r}
fit = lm(price ~ stars + borough, data = nyc_airbnb)
```

```{r}
fit 
summary(fit) 
coef(fit)
fitted.values(fit)
resid(fit) 

names(fit)
names(summary(fit))
```

most of this output is bad, but sometimes its okay 

```{r}
broom::tidy(fit) |>
select(-std.error) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

broom::glance(fit)
```

change reference category

```{r}
nyc_airbnb |>
  mutate(
    borough = fct_infreq(borough)
  ) |>
  lm(price ~ stars + borough, data = _)

broom::tidy(fit) |>
  select(-std.error, -statistic) |>
  mutate(term = str_replace(term, "borough", "Borough:")) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3) 
```

## Diagnostics 

diagnostics is basically "looking at the residuals" 

```{r}
modelr::spread_residuals(nyc_airbnb, fit) 
```

so we can look at residuals 

```{r}
nyc_airbnb |>
  modelr::add_residuals(fit) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = stars, y = resid)) +
  geom_point()

nyc_airbnb |>
  modelr::add_residuals(fit) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = stars, y = resid)) +
  geom_violin()
```

## Hypothesis testing 

```{r}
broom::tidy(fit) |>
  mutate(term = str_replace(term, "borough", "Borough: ")) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

try testing nested models 

```{r}
fit_null = lm(price ~ stars, data = nyc_airbnb)
fit_alt = lm(price ~ stars + borough, data = nyc_airbnb) 

anova(fit_null, fit_alt)
```
## Nesting data

different from fitting nested models
nest data and then fit models to each thing seperately 

try a complicated model 

```{r}
nyc_airbnb |>
  lm(price ~ stars * borough + room_type * borough, data = _) |>
broom::tidy() |>
knitr::kable(digits = 3) 
```
This is a hassle, instead we could do 

to find out whats happening in manhatan 

```{r}
nyc_airbnb |>
  filter(borough == "Manhattan") |>
  lm(price ~ stars + room_type, data = _) |>
  broom::tidy()
```
to find out whats happening in Bronx

```{r}
nyc_airbnb |>
  filter(borough == "Bronx") |>
  lm(price ~ stars + room_type, data = _) |>
  broom::tidy()
```

lets fix this with iteration as we want to fit the same model to different boroughs 

```{r}
airbnb_lm = function(data) {
    
  lm(price ~ stars + room_type, data = data)
  
}
```


```{r}
nyc_airbnb |>
  nest(datasets = -borough) |>
  mutate(
  fits = map(datasets, airbnb_lm),
  results = map(fits, broom::tidy)
) |>
  select(-datasets, -fits) |>
  unnest(results) |>
  select(borough, term, estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = term, 
    values_from = estimate
  )
```
creating the function inside of the code instead of before like previously in this markdown

```{r}
nyc_airbnb |>
  nest(datasets = -borough) |>
  mutate(
  fits = map(datasets, \(data) lm(price ~ stars, data = data)),
  results = map(fits, broom::tidy)
) |>
  select(-datasets, -fits) |>
  unnest(results) |>
  select(borough, term, estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = term, 
    values_from = estimate
  )
```
```{r}
nyc_airbnb |>
  filter(borough == "Manhattan") |>
  nest(datasets = -neighbourhood) |>
  mutate(
    fits = map(datasets, \(df) lm(price ~ stars + room_type, data = df)),
    results = map(fits, broom::tidy)
  ) |>
  select(neighbourhood, results) |>
  unnest(results) |>
  filter(term == "room_typePrivate room") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = neighbourhood, y = estimate)) +
  geom_point() + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 80, hjust =1))
```
